solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Secure pieces of furniture, when relocating south

indicators.note: relocating says a letter of the furniture word shifts to a new position

parts.note: tables are pieces of furniture
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Someone moving house wonders how to keep their furniture safe on the drive south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when relocating' moves the S of TABLES from the back to the front, giving STABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is firmly fixed and steady, which is what secure means as an adjective.

clue.text: Viewed spread, when discussing kitchenware

indicators.note: discussing is talking, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: viewed is saw and spread is span, together SAW SPAN

explanation.surface: A picture of someone admiring a buffet while chatting about pots and pans.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, SAW SPAN runs together into the sound of the cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pan with a handle used for boiling and making sauces is an example of kitchenware.

clue.text: Way out is about 1.6 kilometres away

definitions.meaning: way out means badly wrong, far from the mark
a mile is about 1.6 km, so this is literally that distance away

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a wildly wrong guess; the other is the literal distance, since a mile is about 1.6 km.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a guess that is badly wrong also literally means a single mile distant.

clue.text: Can money satisfy textile manufacturer

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, a loo

explanation.surface: A question of whether cash can keep a mill owner happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'satisfy' is a link meaning the wordplay will supply the answer; 'can' as toilet is US and British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A weaving frame turns thread into cloth, so a machine like this manufactures textiles.

clue.text: Writer's computing work schedule? Wrong way round, using copier

parts.note: the writer's means the setter is: I'M
IT, information technology, is computing

indicators.note: the wrong way round says the schedule word is written backwards

parts.note: a rota is a work schedule

explanation.surface: An office worker complains that a colleague's IT rota has been copied back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong way round' turns ROTA into ATOR to finish the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier is someone who mimics others, the same person as one who imitates.

clue.text: Children's author's maintaining high speed, vital here in Bucks

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the author's name holds the other pieces

parts.note: A. A. Milne wrote Winnie-the-Pooh; with the 's he gives MILNES
a ton is slang for 100 mph, a high speed
key means vital, essential

explanation.surface: A claim that a children's writer keeps up a rapid pace in a vital spot in the county.
explanation.walkthrough: TON and KEY go inside MILNES. Bucks is Buckinghamshire, an English county; the answer is its large new town.
explanation.definitionFit: The new town in question lies in Buckinghamshire, so it is a place found in that county.

clue.text: Book about wanderings from French composer written in language not unknown

indicators.note: written in says the composer's name is set inside the other word
not unknown says a letter for an unknown quantity is dropped

parts.note: a tongue is a language
Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: A description of a travel book drawn from a French composer's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' drops N (a mathematical unknown) from TONGUE, leaving TOGUE; RAVEL goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelogue is a film or book describing someone's journeys, i.e. an account of their roaming.

clue.text: Boxes frantically, vest in coating of sweat when it's over

indicators.note: in says the reworked garment goes inside the other letters
over says the pair of outside letters is turned around
the coating of a word is its outside letters
frantically signals the letters are mixed up wildly

explanation.surface: A boxer sweats so hard that the vest is drenched when the fight is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The outside of 'sweat' is ST, which 'when it's over' turns to TS; 'frantically' gives VSET from 'vest', which goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Television sets are colloquially called boxes in Britain, as in 'the box'.

clue.text: Hard to avoid plant-sucking insects by river — in this section?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the river letter sits beside the rest
to avoid says a letter is left out

parts.note: aphids are plant-sucking insects
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Gardening advice to avoid greenfly by planting near the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'river' in the wordplay: a stretch of fast water is a section of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapids are a fast-flowing stretch of river, the part a canoeist would be in.

clue.text: Agreement about new seaman in uniform

indicators.note: about says the run of pieces is turned around

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman
U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A deal is struck over a new sailor in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns N + OS + IN + U backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting in complete accord, together as one.

clue.text: Makes a big proft, putting tips inside small container

indicators.note: inside says the first pieces go within the container word

parts.note: a cup is a container
tips means leans, as in tilts

explanation.surface: A waiter makes a killing by putting tips in a small jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proft' is a typo for profit as held.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up is an idiom for making a lot of money.

clue.text: Rising numbers residing with giant rat here in Australia

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the pieces read upwards

parts.note: big means giant
to rat is to desert

explanation.surface: Numbers of giant rats are growing in some Australian place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns NOS and BIG upwards to make GIBSON; 'residing with' joins it to DESERT.
explanation.definitionFit: This large desert lies in Western Australia, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: Pitcher's terrible throw fnally ending in home run

indicators.note: a misspelling of finally, taking the last letters of the two words
ending in takes the last letter of the word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A baseball pitcher's bad throw ends in a home run.
explanation.walkthrough: The baseball pitcher and home run are a false scene; a pitcher here is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is a large jug, which is what a ewer is.

clue.text: Performed some of dance stoned, grabbing debauched man

indicators.note: grabbing means holding, so the first word takes the second inside

parts.note: stoned fruit has had its stones removed: pitted
a roué is a debauched man

explanation.surface: Some of the dancers were stoned and grabbed a lecherous man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoned' is not drugged but de-stoned, as cherries.
explanation.definitionFit: To pirouette is to spin on one foot, a move performed as part of a dance.

clue.text: Put before all, port is used in religious ceremony by priest

indicators.note: by means beside, so the priest's letter sits next to the rest

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a port

indicators.note: used in says the small word is put inside the ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a religious ceremony

explanation.surface: Port wine is served in a church service by a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: IS goes inside RITE to make RITISE, after P and RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: To prioritise something is to put it first, ahead of everything else.

clue.text: Dotty was on safari — beginning in Kenya, to the best of my understanding

definitions.text: to the best of my understanding

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: beginning in takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An eccentric relative on safari begins her trip in Kenya, as far as the speaker knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' scrambles WASONSAFARI together with K, the first letter of 'Kenya'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hedge meaning 'to my knowledge', what the speaker believes is true.

clue.text: Left behind violin when hosting new low-level classes

indicators.note: hosting means having as guests inside, so the violin holds the others

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin
D and E are the lowest UK socio-economic grades

explanation.surface: Someone left behind a violin while hosting new beginners' classes.
explanation.walkthrough: UK social grades run A, B, C1, C2, D, E, so D and E are the lower classes.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stranded is to be left behind with no way of getting away.

clue.text: Filmmaker tense around collar

indicators.note: around says the first word goes round the second

parts.note: taut means tense
a ruff is a frilled collar

explanation.surface: A tense film director fiddles with his collar.
explanation.walkthrough: François Truffaut was a French New Wave film director.
explanation.definitionFit: Truffaut was a celebrated French director, an example of a filmmaker.

clue.text: Ivory Merchant? One might get a reward after shooting

definitions.meaning: playfully, someone hunting elephants for valuable tusks chases a rich bounty, with a nod to the film company Merchant Ivory

definitions.text: One might get a reward after shooting
definitions.meaning: a hunter of wanted outlaws is paid a reward after shooting them

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is whimsical: an ivory dealer pursues tusks as bounty, flipping the film-makers Merchant Ivory.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tracks down fugitives for a cash reward, as in Westerns, is this kind of hunter.

clue.text: Rock, rhythm & blues primarily impresses bloke

indicators.note: impresses means presses into, so the picked letters are set inside

parts.note: a bloke is a male

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letters of the words

explanation.surface: Rhythm and blues makes an impression on a man who loves rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like music beside rhythm and blues but is the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Marble is a metamorphic stone, so it is a kind of rock.

clue.text: Increase capital endlessly on vacation in Ukraine

indicators.note: endlessly says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Accra is the capital of Ghana

indicators.note: vacation empties the word, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Capital keeps growing without end while someone holidays in Ukraine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ACCRA to ACCR; Ukraine emptied gives UE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrue is to grow or build up over time, as interest does.

clue.text: Greek excitedly reads about percussion instrument

indicators.note: about says the mixed letters go round the instrument
excitedly signals the letters are shaken up

parts.note: a chime is a percussion instrument

explanation.surface: A Greek reads excitedly about a percussion instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' turns READS into ARDES, which goes round CHIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes was a famous Greek mathematician, an example of a Greek.

clue.text: Rubbish bin aroma latterly very strong

indicators.note: latterly takes the last letters of the words

parts.note: FF is fortissimo, very loud, in music

explanation.surface: The smell from the bin has become very strong lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' is British slang for poor taste, not litter; the bin is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tacky or worthless, which is what rubbish means as an adjective.

clue.text: In front of mother, lifted winning cat

indicators.note: in front of says the first piece comes before the second
lifted in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: up means ahead, winning
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A winning cat is held aloft in front of its mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns UP into PU.
explanation.definitionFit: A puma is a big wild American feline, an example of a cat.

clue.text: German barrels regularly near ship

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word

parts.note: a liner is a ship

explanation.surface: German barrels are stacked regularly near a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Regular letters of 'near' are ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Berlin is a Berliner, an example of a German.

clue.text: Cold plain fish containing bones

indicators.note: containing says the fish word holds the other

parts.note: a tuna is a fish
bones, or sawbones, is slang for a doctor, DR

explanation.surface: A fish on a cold plain still has its bones in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bones' is a doctor, from 'sawbones'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the treeless frozen plain of Arctic regions.

clue.text: Canines still in periphery to explore the ground

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
the periphery of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: yet means still

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Dogs are still on the edge, exploring the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: YET goes inside E...E from 'explore'; 'ground' turns THE into ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeteeth is another name for the canine teeth in the upper jaw.

clue.text: Shakespeare regressive to actress

parts.note: Shakespeare is the Bard

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the small word is turned around

explanation.surface: Shakespeare backs an actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressive' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigitte Bardot is a French film actress.
